name: Bangabandhu Memorial Museum
description: The former residence of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman at Dhanmondi 32, preserved as a museum documenting his life and the birth of Bangladesh.

name: Liberation War Museum
description: A museum dedicated to the 1971 Liberation War, showcasing artefacts, photographs, and stories of the freedom struggle.

name: Bangladesh National Museum
description: The largest museum in Bangladesh, housing collections spanning natural history, art, and the country's cultural heritage.

name: Curzon Hall
description: A striking example of Indo-Saracenic architecture on the Dhaka University campus, built in the early 20th century.

name: Rose Garden Palace
description: A 19th-century zamindar-era palace in Old Dhaka noted for its ornate architecture and historical significance.

name: Bara Katra
description: A 17th-century Mughal-era caravanserai in Old Dhaka, one of the city's oldest surviving structures.

name: Armenian Church
description: A well-preserved 18th-century church in Old Dhaka reflecting the city's historic Armenian trading community.

name: Baldha Garden
description: A century-old botanical garden in Old Dhaka home to a rich variety of rare and exotic plant species.

name: Himchari National Park
description: A hilly national park along the Cox's Bazar coastline known for waterfalls, forest trails, and sea views.

name: Inani Beach
description: A quieter stretch of Cox's Bazar's coastline known for coral fragments and calmer surroundings.

name: Cox's Bazar Marine Drive
description: A scenic coastal road connecting Cox's Bazar to Teknaf, offering uninterrupted views of the Bay of Bengal.

name: Teknaf
description: The southernmost tip of mainland Bangladesh, bordered by hills, sea, and the Naf River.

name: Chimbuk Hill
description: One of the highest points accessible by road in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, popular for panoramic views.

name: Buddha Dhatu Jadi (Golden Temple)
description: The largest Buddhist temple in Bangladesh, home to a sacred Buddha relic, overlooking Bandarban town.

name: Kaptai Lake
description: The largest man-made lake in Bangladesh, formed by the Karnaphuli hydroelectric dam, ringed by hills.

name: Rangamati Hanging Bridge
description: An iconic suspension footbridge over Kaptai Lake and a signature symbol of Rangamati.

name: Alutila Cave
description: A natural limestone cave in the hills of Khagrachhari, explored with torches through its dark, winding tunnel.

name: Richhang Waterfall
description: A tiered waterfall tucked in the hills near Khagrachhari town, reachable by a short hillside trek.

name: Lalakhal
description: Known for its striking turquoise-blue river water, framed by hills and betel-nut plantations.

name: Hakaluki Haor
description: One of the largest wetlands in Bangladesh, a vital habitat for migratory birds and freshwater fish.

name: Bholaganj (Volaganj)
description: A stone-collection area near the India border, known for its clear streams and quarry-carved landscape.

name: Shrine of Hazrat Shah Jalal
description: The shrine of the revered Sufi saint Hazrat Shah Jalal, one of the most visited religious sites in Sylhet.

name: Shrine of Hazrat Shah Paran
description: A historic Sufi shrine on the outskirts of Sylhet city, dedicated to Hazrat Shah Paran.

name: Guthia Mosque
description: A century-old mosque in Barisal noted for its terracotta ornamentation and colonial-era architecture.

name: Durga Sagar
description: An 18th-century excavated lake surrounded by palm trees, one of the largest ponds in southern Bangladesh.

name: Michael Madhusudan Dutta's House
description: The ancestral home of the pioneering 19th-century Bengali poet Michael Madhusudan Dutta, now a memorial site.

name: Khan Jahan Ali's Tomb
description: The mausoleum of Khan Jahan Ali, the Sufi saint who founded the historic city of Bagerhat.

name: Varendra Research Museum
description: The oldest museum in Bangladesh, holding archaeological artefacts from the ancient Varendra region.

name: Padma Garden
description: A riverside park along the Padma in Rajshahi city, popular for sunset views over the river.

name: Natore Rajbari (Uttara Gono Bhaban)
description: A grand 18th-century zamindar palace complex, now used as the President's northern residence and a heritage site.

name: Chalan Beel
description: One of the largest wetlands in Bangladesh, spanning several districts and rich in freshwater biodiversity.

name: Bhawal National Park
description: A sal-forest national park near Dhaka, popular for day trips, forest trails, and picnicking.

name: Nuhash Palli
description: A private retreat created by novelist Humayun Ahmed, now a memorial garden open to visitors.

name: Shashi Lodge
description: A 19th-century zamindar mansion in Mymensingh town, known for its colonial-era architecture.

name: Birishiri
description: A scenic area along the Someshwari River, known for china-clay hills and views towards the Meghalaya border.

name: Gajni Avinjan Kendra
description: An eco-tourism spot at the foothills of the Garo Hills, popular for its scenery and adventure activities.
